sections.name: Hook
lines: bt_hook
Your earbuds and your phone are having a conversation that jumps channels sixteen hundred times a second.
bt_title
Here's how that tiny wireless link works, in five steps.

sections.name: Short-range radio
lines: bt_radio
Step one. Bluetooth is radio, in the same two point four gigahertz band as Wi-Fi, but much weaker, so it usually reaches just a few metres.
bt_power
That low power is the point. It saves battery for tiny gadgets, like earbuds, watches and keyboards.

sections.name: Hopping channels
lines: bt_crowd
Step two. That band is crowded, with Wi-Fi, microwaves and other gadgets all shouting at once.
bt_hop
So classic Bluetooth splits it into seventy-nine channels, and hops between them sixteen hundred times every second.
bt_dodge
If one channel is noisy, the next hop dodges it. Both devices follow the same hopping pattern, so they stay in step.

sections.name: Pairing
lines: bt_pair
Step three. The first time you connect, the devices pair. They swap secret keys, and remember each other.
bt_reconnect
After that, they find each other automatically, and what they send is encrypted.

sections.name: Sending sound
lines: bt_codec
Step four. Raw audio is too much data for Bluetooth, so the sound is squeezed down by a codec, then unpacked in your ears.
bt_delay
All that packing and hopping adds a tiny delay, which is why video can look slightly out of sync with the sound.

sections.name: Low energy
lines: bt_ble
Step five. Bluetooth Low Energy sends tiny bursts of data, then sleeps. That's how a tracker tag can run for about a year on a coin battery.
bt_name
And the name? It comes from a Viking king, Harald Bluetooth, who united Denmark. The logo is his initials, in runes.

sections.name: Recap
lines: w_recap
Weak radio. Seventy-nine channels, hopping in step. Pairing swaps keys, codecs squeeze the sound, and Low Energy sleeps between bursts.
outro
Next time your earbuds connect, picture them hopping in perfect step. Follow for more of the tech you use every day.
